mainEntity.name: Do Verde Valley temperature swings affect interior drywall in metal structures?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Verde Valley, the primary challenge is managing extreme temperature swings between scorching summers and freezing winter nights. In places like Cottonwood, Camp Verde, and Clarkdale, wide daily thermal variations cause steel roof purlins and wall panels to expand and contract constantly. If interior walls are tied directly into rigid roof beams without deflection tracks or slip connections, that expansion will push down on the interior framing and cause visible drywall cracking. Ensuring that your framing accommodates structural thermal movement and incorporating adequate cavity insulation prevents seasonal shifting and keeps air conditioning and heating costs manageable year-round.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, large temperature shifts cause steel to expand and contract; framing must use deflection tracks or isolated walls so structural movement does not crack the drywall.
